results.title: Why is the Dollar higher in value than the Rupee?
excerpts:
[](https://unacademy.com/)

* 

*

Search for:

) Join for Free

The Indian Rupee is valued less compared to the US Dollar. The value of one Dollar to one Indian Rupee fluctuates, referred to as the exchange rate. In the global foreign exchange market, the exchange rate changes every day, and it is an essential indicator of a country’s economic strength. Imports become more expensive as the value of a foreign currency rises, whereas exports become less expensive.

The US Dollar is higher than the Rupee for various reasons. India imports commodities from the US instead of exporting on its own which is why the value of the Dollar is high due to the number of exports. Under this circumstance, the demand for Dollars rises since the US will receive more cash inflow in the form of Dollars because of the positive balance of purchase and the balance of the **capital account** .

## **The Flow Of Foreign Capital**

...

A country usually invests its funds abroad for a certain period of time and it is referred to as net capital outflow. It means that the country invests abroad more than it invests in its own nation. In simple terms outflow can be defined as the capital taken out of the country for buying foreign assets. Savings minus investment is considered as capital outflow.

Foreign direct investment entails actively managing the assets or interest purchased, whereas portfolio investment does not require management involvement.

In this circumstance, demand for the US Dollar will initially increase as more Dollars will be paid to the US when purchasing goods from them. More Dollars will have to be obtained on the Indian foreign exchange market in order to pay for any item.

As a result, an open economy can purchase and sell assets on the financial market, resulting in capital flow.
When there is a positive net capital outflow, residents buy more foreign assets than foreigners acquire domestic assets. When the index is negative, foreigners buy more domestic holdings than locals.

## **The Reason Why the Dollar is Higher Than the Rupee**

The Dollar is the most demanded currency in the world because of heavy exports to different nations. One of the reasons why the Rupee is cheaper than the Dollar is because of India’s fiscal deficit. The use of crude oil, rise of gold prices, the boom of Chinese imports, Indians going for US tours, imported cars, electronics etc. are some of the reasons why the Dollar is higher than Rupee.

Value of any currency depends on its demand in the market. The US is the biggest economy in the world and contributes to around 25% of the world economy. Most of the crude oil and important sources of energy is traded through Dollars. Furthermore, the US has the highest number of MNCs and has major trade relations with other countries.
## **Conclusion**

The demand for the Dollar is higher in those countries which import more than it exports. India, for example, imports more than it exports which is why 1 USD is currently worth 73.28 INR, and the value keeps on changing every minute. Smaller and less industrial countries like the Bahamas, where 1 Bahamian Dollar equals 1 USD, have this relation because they are less reliant on imports such as crude oil, whereas India imports crude oil in excessive quantities. A currency’s value sometimes is not an accurate indicator of its economic health; other aspects include low inflation, good GDP, and suitable employment.

#### What is the Indian Rupee (INR)?

The Indian rupee, symbolized by ₹, is the official currency of India and one of the most traded currencies in Asia. Known for its dynamic role in the fast-growing Indian economy, INR reflects the country's diverse economic sectors. The currency's value can be volatile, influenced by government policies and economic reforms. This makes it crucial for regional trade and investment.

#### What is the US Dollar (USD)?

The United States dollar, symbolized by $, is the official currency of the United States and the world’s primary reserve currency.
As the most traded currency globally, it plays a central role in international trade and finance, serving as a preferred medium for global reserves held by governments and institutions. This status as a reserve currency means that many countries hold USD as part of their foreign exchange reserves, which enhances its stability and liquidity. The USD is known for its stability, liquidity, and widespread use in global transactions. Its dominance in Forex markets and its role as a benchmark in the global economy underscore its significance, particularly in trade with major partners such as China, the European Union, and Japan.
